svg.text: v6 — Document ingestion and keyword search
PROBLEM: a "knowledge" platform with no knowledge — nowhere to store a document, nothing to read a file, nothing to find a passage.
FIX: upload → extract → ~800-char overlapping chunks → PostgreSQL with a tsvector + GIN index. Keyword search is the BASELINE embeddings must beat.
PATH A — INGEST: POST /documents
multipart/form-data file=refund-policy.pdf Authorization: Bearer eyJ…
.txt / .md / .pdf, ≤ 5 MB, ≤ 300 pages
core/request_limits.py — middleware, BEFORE auth
Content-Length > 5 MB + 64 KB → 413 from the header alone (0 body bytes read)
Found by measuring: body parsed before auth
Anonymous 200 MB upload → received in full → 401
after 4,146 ms. Now: 413 in 1.4–3.2 ms.
Chunked uploads (no Content-Length) still bypass — proxy's job.
get_current_user → limit_ingestion (20/min per user) → documents/router.py
Its own budget: a burst of uploads cannot lock a user out of classifying tickets.
documents/service.py — SHA-256 of the bytes
Already stored in this organisation? 409 — before any extraction. Unique (organization_id, sha256) closes the race.
documents/extraction.py → documents/chunking.py
type from name AND first bytes ("%PDF-") · pypdf · strip NUL · no text → 422
split at paragraph → sentence → word, ≤ 800 chars, 100 chars overlap, exact offsets
documents/repository.py → PostgreSQL, ONE transaction
documents (1 row: title, organization_id, content, sha256)
document_chunks (N rows: text, search_vector GENERATED, GIN index)
The cost: ingestion runs INSIDE the request
txt 10 KB 165 ms
txt 1 MB 2,372 ms (1,737 chunks)
txt 4.9 MB 8,406 ms (8,518 chunks)
pdf 100 pages 3,594 ms (extract 2.5 s)
pdf 300 pages 5,774 ms
P50 POST /documents. The worker serves nothing else meanwhile.
201 {"id": 12, "title": "Refund policy", "chunk_count": 14}
PATH B — FIND: GET /documents/search?q=how long does a refund take
service.py — keep [a-z0-9] words only (max 32)
tsquery operators never pass through: "refund') | !(x" is harmless; no words → 422
repository.py — one SQL query
WHERE organization_id = 3 AND search_vector @@ 'how | long | refund | take'
ORDER BY ts_rank(...) DESC LIMIT 5 (stems: refunds → refund)
[{"document_title": "Refund policy", "chunk_index": 0, "text": "Refunds are…"}]
ts_rank, chosen by measurement
First choice ts_rank_cd ranks every MATCHING chunk
before LIMIT. At 39,588 chunks, common words:
ts_rank_cd 5,909 ms → ts_rank 108 ms
Evaluation no worse: hit@3 0.73 both, MRR 0.64 → 0.66.
Synthetic 50-word corpus: ~95% of chunks match — a worst case.
MEASURED LOCALLY — RETRIEVAL BASELINE, 20 ARTICLES, 30 QUESTIONS, match=any, ts_rank
"How do I reset my password?"
An upper bound: articles and questions
were written by the same author.
"Can I get my money back?" → nothing
hit@3 0.47 · MRR 0.31 · 20% empty
Every miss is a vocabulary mismatch:
"admin" vs "Administrators", "forget" vs "erase".
word in no chunk: GIN Bitmap Scan 0.356 ms
20-chunk org: org-id Index Scan 0.517 ms
95% of chunks match: Seq Scan 84.6 ms
GIN declined when it selects almost everything.
1. Keyword search does not understand meaning: paraphrase hit@3 0.47, 20% return nothing → EMBEDDINGS (v8) + vector search (v9), compared on the same 30 questions.
2. Ingestion blocks the request: 300-page PDF 5.8 s, 4.9 MB text 8.4 s per upload → BACKGROUND PROCESSING (v7): accept, return 202, extract in a worker.
3. Search cost grows with the number of MATCHING chunks, not with limit — v3's problem, inside the database. 4. Originals not kept (ADR-019).
5. Streamed uploads without Content-Length bypass the size check. 6. English-only stemming. 7. Test suite 187 s (180 tests).
All numbers: one session, DB_ECHO=false, no --reload, httpx client, PostgreSQL 17 in Docker on a Windows 11 laptop.
